**Review result:** I find no source-level blocker to the proposed one-time, zero-file `--bootstrap-check`, subject to the controlled invocation and reporting conditions below. This is an endorsement of that bounded attempt, not a claim that initialization will succeed on Windows or that the dormant controller is ready for use.

The reviewed identity is commit `c5e01df9d4a06fa6184841cb30d22ec539e30590`. HEAD matched it, the worktree was clean, and `ebf71ce713e4d71a2b32193fd360cfda3cd1dab9` is an ancestor. I read all six requested files and both prior review artifacts.

The four requested repairs are present:

- [run_fixture.py](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/run_fixture.py:32) retains the verified Git blob bytes and passes those bytes to transport construction; it does not reread the controller pathname. The proposed inline loader must execute the exact committed driver bytes with the stated `__file__`, `__name__`, and arguments.
- [Controller.ps1](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/Controller.ps1:266) preserves all four exit-code bytes through `BitConverter`, including values with the high bit set.
- The controller checks the deadline after cleanup observations and again before requesting watchdog cancellation.
- The normal timeout report says guest command completion is unknown. The README correctly identifies process creation as outside the interruptible response deadline.

The bootstrap source decompresses and hashes the controller in memory, defines its functions, emits and checks native/layout/watchdog types, queries `IsWow64Process2` for the current process, and checks the two specified assembly names in the runtime directory. I found no explicit bootstrap path that invokes the controller lifecycle, starts its watchdog, creates a Job or guest file, launches a compiler or fixture/helper, or changes policy. Assembly flags establish existence only at those two runtime-directory paths; they do not establish compiler presence or compatibility.

Two limitations need to accompany the attempt:

1. **Exceptional local teardown can escape the normal timeout report.** At [run_fixture.py:151](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/run_fixture.py:151), a failure of `kill()` or the five-second `wait()` can leave the saved report without the normal unknown-completion limitation; the `Popen` context may also wait further. Treat every timeout, exception, or incomplete response as **guest completion UNKNOWN**, and do not represent five seconds as an absolute teardown bound. This reporting limitation does not introduce a guest-side action in the proposed bootstrap.
2. **The dormant watchdog deadline still has a scheduling race.** At [Controller.ps1:291](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/Controller.ps1:291), the thread can be delayed after its final time check and signal the stop event after the deadline; the watchdog checks that event before checking elapsed time. The added checks establish the requested observations but do not make cancellation atomic with the deadline. Resolve and independently verify that lifecycle before any future use; it is not invoked by this bootstrap.

Namespace admission remains refused under the documented sharing-only conflict. The full native suite remains **NOT RUN**. I made no writes, ran no host tests, and made no guest contact; PowerShell initialization, emitted IL execution, API availability, watchdog behavior, cleanup, and fixture behavior remain unverified on Windows. This review makes no acceptance or production-policy decision.
